title: Compliance Policy on Personal Sending Limits — Personal Sender Account
content:
**Policy clause.** The sending limits of the Personal Sender Account level in force at the moment of booking apply to every personal transfer the customer books, whatever the delivery method (Bank Deposit, Cash Pickup, Mobile Wallet); the booking rules of each delivery method apply them to each booking. A personal transfer is within limits only when all six of the following hold:

1. its principal does not exceed the level's largest single transfer;
2. its principal plus the principal of the personal transfers already booked in the rolling 24 hours does not exceed the level's 24-hour ceiling;
3. its principal plus the principal of the personal transfers already booked in the rolling 30 calendar days does not exceed the level's 30-day ceiling;
4. its principal plus the principal of the personal transfers already booked in the rolling 180 calendar days does not exceed the level's 180-day ceiling;
5. the number of personal transfers already booked in the rolling 24 hours is below the level's transfer count;
6. the transfer's corridor is already among the corridors sent to in the rolling 30 calendar days, or the number of those corridors is below the level's corridor count.

(Each level's largest single transfer, ceilings and counts are the sending limits set for that level of the Personal Sender Account.)

## What is counted

- **Principal only.** Limits count the principal in USD; transfer fees, card surcharges and exchange-rate margins are never counted.
- **Which transfers.** The customer's personal transfers in Bank Deposit, Cash Pickup and Mobile Wallet on this Personal Sender Account. Transfers whose status is cancelled or refunded drop out of every window; a returned, expired or failed transfer still counts until it is refunded. Sending through a Paloma Business account is never counted here.
- **The windows.** The rolling 24 hours covers transfers booked strictly later than 24 hours before the handling moment. The rolling 30 calendar days covers transfers booked on the handling date or any of the 29 calendar days before it; the rolling 180 calendar days covers the handling date and the 179 calendar days before it. The corridor count is the number of distinct corridors among the same transfers in the rolling 30 calendar days.
- **Equality.** Equality with a ceiling is within limits.

## When a booking would exceed a ceiling

A booking that would exceed any ceiling is not made. The customer may lower the amount, wait until earlier transfers leave the window, or reach a higher level through an agent-applied upgrade or a compliance limit review. Splitting one payment into several transfers, or across other people's accounts, to stay under a ceiling is structuring and is never assisted.

## Level changes

A level change takes effect at once: transfers booked after the date the new level took effect are measured against the new ceilings, and transfers already booked are never re-checked.

## Worked check (hypothetical figures)

A customer at Paloma Verified (largest single transfer 2999.00 USD, 30-day ceiling 10000.00 USD) has 7500.00 USD of principal on transfers booked in the last 30 calendar days, of which one transfer of 500.00 USD was cancelled.

| Proposed principal | Counted 30-day total with it | Within the 30-day ceiling? |
|---|---|---|
| 2999.00 | 7000.00 plus 2999.00, that is 9999.00 | yes |
| 3000.00 | — | no: exceeds the largest single transfer of 2999.00 |
| 2500.00 | 7000.00 plus 2500.00, that is 9500.00 | yes |

The cancelled 500.00 USD drops out, so 7000.00 USD is counted. The 3000.00 USD transfer fails condition 1 whatever the windows show. The other conditions (24-hour total, transfer count, corridors) must hold as well; the figures above test only conditions 1 and 3.
